The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

  1. I have received your letters, especially the last one about the mattress. I hope you have received it by now.

  2. I would have liked to hear of new cases of nursing; let us hope that the good Jesus will deign to let himself be nursed by the poor daughters of his great Grandmother Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate.1

  3. Daughter, courage and patience; you will see that the Lord will soon come with special providence. I can assure you that I am deeply grieved by this want and scarcity of providence, and my anxiety is such that my chest feels crushed between two stones; yet my trust in God the Father does not fail in the least. When we least expect it, he will provide.2 Let us pray fervently so that our prayers may reach the loving heart of Jesus; that is where the source of all riches, both spiritual and temporal, is found.

  1. See to the observance of the holy Rule, another most powerful means of having the Eternal Father's right hand favourable to us.3 Dear hand, which heals all our wounds wherever it points its gentle finger.

  2. Daughter, love this dear Eternal Father and have your daughters love him; if they love this God the Father, our one and only good, they will become perfect and can do whatever they like, for everything will be done well.

  3. A line to all:4 My blessed daughters, stand firm and full of trust in God. Embrace and love your privations, the discomfort your poor human nature must bear; treasure them and joyfully offer them to your Eternal Father, that he may deign to accept and keep them, changing them into some little treasure of his own.

  4. What delight, daughters, to think that for so little suffering you will have great joy, and your heart will feel in advance the joy of its Beloved's love and you will experience immense delight. God grant you may taste this honey of suffering, which is the essence of every good.

  5. I want you to say special prayers for me for a grace I am awaiting, and I want you to devote the whole month of June to this and direct all your prayers to the precious Blood of Jesus, offering it to the Eternal Father so that he may grant me the grace I desire, and five Our Fathers to the Crucifix.5 God bless you and pour out on you his choicest blessings.

Goodbye, I am your Poor Mother

Rosa Gattorno

She apologises for the delay and reports on the running of the school, the pupils who attend it and the help they receive.1

[Most Illustrious Excellency]

  1. I am most distressed to have obliged Your Lordship to write a second letter to obtain the information you asked for in yours of the 13th. The reason was my absence from this house for a few days, so that I only received your letter yesterday. Please excuse this involuntary omission.

  2. The nursery, or rather the shelter, which we keep open in Via della Morte takes in very poor children whose parents, precisely because of their poverty, cannot provide them with decent clothes or what they need to attend the city's elementary schools. We take them into our shelter and give them free every day soup, exercise books, books, pens, school necessities and often clothes as well.

  3. We have no regular classes, because they come to us at all times of the year and not all with the same level of schooling, so that one might say each pupil forms a class on his own.

  4. We accept them from three to eight; after that their parents send them to the De Cesaris Cella workroom, where they are taught by special teachers and then sit the final examination.

  5. This is the state of the Nursery that our Institute keeps open at its own expense.2

With the greatest respect I remain

[Your most devoted Sr. A. M. Rosa Gattorno]

In a few days she leaves for Rome. They should go on praying that she may obtain the little house Rosa promised. At her audience with the Holy Father she will ask a special blessing for them.

A.M.F. Dear to God,

  1. A line to tell you that on Saturday1 I leave for Rome. The longed-for permission has come; thank you, and please pray hard that I may obtain everything, especially the little House dear Rosa promised me, as you assured me.23 I am going in the certainty of getting it; you pray the Most High to inspire the one who is to give it to me.

  2. I promise you that if you obtain for me speedy permission for a private audience with the Holy Father, I will ask a special blessing for you.

  3. So pray and have others pray. Some sacrifice offered for me by that good Friar; do not stop. I will write as soon as I obtain any of these things, especially the House. Goodbye. I am your poor

Friend Sr. A. M. Rosa Gattorno

Pray that the Lord may send a little providence, for charity's sake.

She announces her imminent departure for Rome. She asks prayers for the journey, though her health is poor, and for a good outcome in the Institute's business. She ends with a prayer for all her daughters, whom she leaves in the heart of Jesus.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

Our daughter,

  1. A line to inform you that tomorrow at noon I leave for Rome.1 Sr. A. Serafina has orders to help you.2 When I get there I will send you my address; have prayers said that I may arrive alive.

  2. Daughter, if I had to consider my body, it would certainly be rash to undertake so long a journey, for, humanly speaking, I have no hope of health any more; but if God so commands, I go, relying on his providence.3

  3. Gather all your Daughters, tell them in confidence and urge them to pray. Better still, read them these two lines: Our daughters,4 I leave for Rome, relying entirely on the mercy of God the Father, that he may give strength to one who has no life. Pray, pray, that when I arrive I may obtain everything our poor Institute needs.

  4. My God! To you I hand over these creatures you have entrusted to me. Now for all this time I place them in the heart of your Son Jesus; cover them with heavenly dew, so that they may be protected in every encounter.5 In this loving retreat of the heart of Jesus may they learn the true school of your divine love.

My God, bless them and strengthen them in suffering. Pour out on them your choicest blessings. Goodbye; I am your affectionate Mother Sr. Anna Maria Rosa

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc231: Her love for God is total. notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc246: In her typically vivid language she expresses fundamental biblical and theological ideas: the temporary nature of suffering (Cf. Rom 8:18) and the eternal joy of Paradise (Cf. Mt 25:23; Rev 21:14).
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc247: Every statement corresponds to firm convictions born and rooted in her through experience: Christ drew her with him onto the cross out of love and as a gift of God's mercy. Therefore suffering is a force of love that unites with Christ.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc248: She adapts to her daughter's moral and spiritual stature so as not to frighten her. God, a merciful Father, takes account of our human limits and knows how to measure the weight we can «comfortably bear».

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc354: This letter survives in an autograph copy by the secretary Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino, who omits the date and the community addressed and simply notes: Letter written by the Mother at Sampierdarena. Given its subject and style, very similar to the instructions she gave the Sampierdarena community in March 1871, it can be dated to that time. As for the community addressed, bearing in mind that in March 1871 there was one at Sampierdarena and two in Piacenza, it seems certainly addressed to the sisters of the «Branch House» — as they called it — in Piacenza, where home nursing was carried out, sick sisters were cared for and the school was being organised. Supporting this is an expression of M. Rosa to Francesca about the nurses: Cf. L 29, 4; Sr. A. Francesca for her part makes some negative remarks about the sisters in her letters of this period.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc369: The portrait of the FSA is complete in its originality: a woman rich in the finest feminine feelings, harmoniously blended in a deep and balanced religious life. In sketching this profile the Mother unconsciously describes herself. Sr. A. Santina Solenghi says of her: «In practising all these virtues (theological and cardinal) she was just and balanced. notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc410: She speaks directly to the sisters of the community, urging them to trust in God and to look with the eyes of faith on their privations, an effective means of growing in love and a source of joy.

Rule '69 p. 25), in the firm certainty that the Father will help her accomplish what he asks; she sets out relying entirely on the mercy of God the Father.

notes.lettere-en-v1-fns237_2: Courage! In comforting the sister she rekindles her faith and finds again, in trust in God, a clear view of her action: for God's Work, with boldness in hope.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fns237_7: My occupations. Of hands and of everything. Not only are they so many that they take all her time every day, but they worry her so much that she wears herself out mentally in the difficult, vain search for solutions.
notes.lettere-en-v1-fns240_2: A word of comfort. Not mere words but the support of spiritual consolation, the gift and fruit of unspeakable, extreme grief. Saint Paul expressed the same experience to the Corinthians: «as we share abundantly in Christ's sufferings, so through Christ we share abundantly in comfort too» (2 Cor 1:5).
notes.lettere-en-v2-fns329_2: Want and scarcity. The words clearly express the poverty already experienced in the other foundations (Cf. Fiocchi I, p. 190 ff). She suffers with her Daughters, taking on their anguish at such insecurity to the point of feeling crushed: my chest feels crushed between two stones. But from the depths rises her plea to the Father for help; her trust in him never fails, and she asks her daughters for extra courage and patience, for by drawing from the source they will receive what they need.
